tools.name: decode
tools.description: Read a package barcode or tracking number (IMpb), or a letter's or flat's Intelligent Mail barcode (IMb) from its digits or bars: its layout, each field's digits and meaning, whether the check digit or the bars' frame check holds, and the service type code's or Service Type ID's row in the USPS list

tools.name: lookup
tools.description: Look up a USPS code: its row as USPS prints it in the newest edition that lists it, the codes its cells name, the editions that list it and its history, each row with its passage id. A code is found without the marks USPS prints around it and in a row USPS prints for several codes: 750 finds *750, 8

tools.name: diff
tools.description: What changed in a code table or document between two editions: each code added, removed or changed and each changed section, rated editorial, additive or breaking, with who rated it.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search the codes, terms, banner texts, specs and documents postalref models, by one index: names and codes whose key is the query's first, then those that start with it, then those with words that start with its words, then codes whose row has its words. tools.name: define
tools.description: What USPS means by a name or abbreviation: each registry entry it names, in the order search ranks them, with its kind and tier, the USPS words that define it and the page they're on, its other names, postalref's own explanation where it has one, and postalref's page about it. tools.name: read_source
tools.description: Read any document postalref holds page by page, as extracted, to quote it: a quote cites the revision's sha256, the PDF page and the words exactly. A text without pages, a web page or a product page, reads in parts, and a quote from one cites no page. Quote whole sentences, word for word, from a pag

tools.name: search_documents
tools.description: Search every document on PostalPro by title and file name, with its page and newest file, and the product pages and downloads postalref holds by title. Each one postalref holds the text of carries an `id`, which read_source takes as `document`. A title says only that USPS publishes a document: read

tools.name: search_text
tools.description: Search the text of every document postalref holds, or of one, for the pages that say the words, best first: those that say them as a phrase, then by how much of the page they are and how many of them it says side by side or close together, a table of contents last. findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "lookup" appears informational but accepts parameters (code) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: read_source, search_text · Private data: diff, search, define, read_source, search_documents, search_text · Public sink: search_text.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: read_source, search_text · Private data: diff, search, define, read_source, search_documents, search_text · Public sink: search_text

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "decode" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
